procedure.description: revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 37227 (revascularization of the femoral-popliteal artery with atherectomy and stent placement) with date of service 2026-07-05. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish limb-threatening ischemia or failure of supervised exercise therapy.

criteria.text: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (ischemic rest pain, non-healing ulcer, or gangrene, Rutherford 4 to 6); or lifestyle-limiting claudication (Rutherford 3) that has failed at least 12 weeks of supervised exercise therapy and optimal medical therapy.
Hemodynamic confirmation: ankle-brachial index 0.4 or less, toe pressure below 30 mmHg, or TcPO2 below 30 mmHg for limb-threatening ischemia (ankle-brachial index below 0.9 for claudication).
Imaging (duplex, CT angiography, or angiography) demonstrating a femoropopliteal stenosis of 50 percent or more, or an occlusion, amenable to endovascular treatment.
Optimal medical therapy documented: an antiplatelet agent, a statin, and smoking cessation or cessation counseling.

chart.text: Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.8, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

Here with a cough and congestion for 5 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 17 and 17. No ocular pathology noted.
A1c came back 6.6. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

65 year old woman referred by podiatry for the right leg. Diabetic 18 years, hypertension, prior carotid endarterectomy. Discussed endovascular versus bypass; endovascular first given the anatomy. Her history otherwise: osteoarthritis of the hands, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 4 years ago, no alcohol, retired. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Right calf cramping at about two blocks that goes away when she stops, no rest pain, no wounds, Rutherford 3. Told her to walk more and gave her the handout; she has not done a supervised exercise program. On aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 80. Quit smoking 10 weeks ago after 34 years; counseled again today and offered nicotine replacement.
Arterial studies. Ankle-brachial index right 0.75, left 0.85. Right toe pressure 57 mmHg. Biphasic waveforms at the right popliteal and tibial levels.
Vitamin D came back 19. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

CT angiography with runoff: right superficial femoral artery occluded over 11 centimeters from the mid thigh to the adductor canal, reconstitution of the above-knee popliteal artery, two-vessel runoff via the anterior tibial and peroneal. Contralateral mild disease. Aortoiliac segments patent.
Blood pressure check. 126 over 78 today, 133 over 79 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.

Back to review the imaging. Plan right superficial femoral artery recanalization with atherectomy and stent, outpatient. Risks reviewed including embolization and need for bypass. Vitals today 136 over 72, pulse 84.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Pre-procedure visit. Creatinine 1.1, hold metformin, hydration protocol. Consent signed.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-1 (indication) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan, a shortfall, or a result below the threshold.
